![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/19d2d5698ad6b22c003b44d1a023c56ae7779a6d26345732bace3723062f6e0d.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,\sqrt{x}\le y\le 2\}.
$$

Notice that the left boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x)$ is

$$
x=0,
$$

and the right boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x),$ is

$$
y=\sqrt{x}\,⟹\,x={y}^{2}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we write $D$ as type II region. Its type II representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/81596115241d43f3935ba9e055a3c748c1c1ae283aa2a6a372492ee8c68170cd.png)

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{3}+\pi )\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{3}+\pi )\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{3}+\pi )[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{3}+\pi )[x]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{3}+\pi )\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{3}+\pi )}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(8+\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(8+\pi )}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
